long_biography.plain_text:
Born in Wibsey, Bradford, Sir Robert Ogden left school at fourteen and worked on a Yorkshire Dales farm before National Service. He used military savings, with help toward a deposit from his mother, to buy an old tipper truck. That haulage venture grew into the Ogden Group, which expanded through demolition, equipment, civil engineering, quarrying, coal recovery and the reclamation of industrial land for redevelopment. The business was built with several of his brothers, but Ogden remained its founder and controlling figure.

Property became a major later focus. Sir Robert Ogden Estates held and developed real estate, and Ogden controlled more than three-quarters of its shares until his death in 2022. He was appointed CBE and later knighted, while supporting medical, educational and disability projects. The Sir Robert Ogden Charitable Foundation is a distinct registered charity: its investments and donated funds are charitable assets, not part of his personal estate or operating-company holdings.

uncertainties.detail: The authoritative owner record incorrectly says Alive. The Gazette and Companies House establish death on 6 March 2022, so mortality status is proposed for correction. Because the immutable input inventory classifies the blank death fields as inapplicable while Alive remains the baseline, the schema's strict proposal guardrail prevents adding death day, month and year in this pending dossier; those fields should be filled after or alongside the reviewed mortality correction.

Sir is correctly stored as the title. Ogden was appointed CBE in 1983 and knighted in 2001; Hon LLD is an honorary degree and is retained in source identity text rather than inserted as a middle name or name suffix.

Several brothers helped build the Ogden Group, but the official biography identifies Robert as its founder and Companies House establishes his personal controlling stake in Sir Robert Ogden Estates. The dossier does not attribute every family-company interest or corporate asset solely to him.

Construction, engineering, quarrying, coal recovery and land reclamation created the original fortune. By Ogden's death, a controlling stake in the real-estate company Sir Robert Ogden Estates was the clearest dominant private holding, supporting Real Estate as the primary industry at death.

Ogden's mother sold her car to help him make the deposit on his first truck, but the evidence shows no inherited core business or substantial family-wealth platform. His own military savings, work and repeated reinvestment drove the enterprise, supporting Self-made — independent start.

The Sir Robert Ogden Charitable Foundation is a separate registered charity. Its cash, investments, donations, grants and any property belong to the charity and are dedicated to its public-benefit objects; they are not personal assets of Ogden, his estate, Lady Ogden or Sir Robert Ogden Estates.

No uniquely verified personal LinkedIn, Instagram, personal website, Wikipedia page or dedicated Forbes.com profile met the acceptance threshold. The official Ogden Group site is proposed as a Company Website; the foundation site remains an organizational source rather than a personal social profile.
